title: Pi Permissions Configuration
description: Policy gates for Pi tools. The sandbox extension (bubblewrap always-on, Gondolin via --sandbox) owns general bash and path-tool isolation at the OS layer; this config owns policy on top. Files: ~/.pi/agent/permissions.json (global) and <cwd>/.pi/permissions.json (project-local), merged with project taking precedence.

$schema.description: URL of this schema. Editors use it for validation/autocomplete.

rules.description: Per-tool permission rules. Each key is a tool name; the value is either a single permission string (applies to every call of that tool) or a glob-pattern object mapping patterns to permissions. Longest matching pattern wins. Files (platform) in path-based tools are resolved against the workspace cwd before matching; bash commands strip the git-interceptor env prefix first.

read.description: Read tool. Patterns match the resolved file path. `cloak` redacts via the matching `masks.read` entry instead of blocking; `deny` blocks the read entirely. Defaults: allow everything, cloak .env files, deny ~/.ssh/keys/.aws/.git/node_modules/venvs/build outputs.

write.description: Write tool. Patterns match the resolved file path. Defaults: allow everything, deny .env/.git/node_modules/venvs.

edit.description: Edit tool. Patterns match the resolved file path. Defaults mirror write.

bash.description: Bash. Patterns match the command string (after stripping the git-interceptor env prefix). ONLY `deny` is effective under the sandbox tiers: allow/ask/cloak are ignored so bash never prompts and subagents (no UI) never hard-block. The sandbox (bubblewrap by default, Gondolin via --sandbox) owns general bash gating; bash rules here are pure policy refinement that survives across all tiers including --no-sandbox. Defaults: curated global denies (sudo, nixos-rebuild, home-manager, darwin-rebuild, shutdown, reboot, poweroff, halt, mkfs, dd if=/dev, fdisk, gdisk, parted, mount, umount, nvram, systemctl reboot/poweroff/halt). Per-repo `.pi/permissions.json` may refine these via longest-pattern-wins (e.g. allow `nixos-rebuild dry-*`).

external_directory.description: Gate for path-based tools (read/write/edit) reaching OUTSIDE the workspace. Patterns match the external directory root (the first directory above the workspace cwd, or the path root for different volumes). `ask` is the one surviving interactive prompt (Yes/No, no Explain); it auto-denies cleanly in non-interactive sessions (subagents). `allow` lets a sibling workspace be touched without prompting (e.g. `~/Documents/**`). Defaults: ask for everything outside the workspace.

webfetch.description: Webfetch is GET-only (web-tools/network.ts hardcodes method: "GET") and has NO default rule, so it is allowed by absence. Setting rules here (e.g. `bash: ?`) only gates the URL string. For network containment use the sandbox tiers: bubblewrap network allow/deny-domains (always-on) or Gondolin VM network policy via --sandbox.

masks.description: Redaction patterns applied to read tool output when the matching `rules.read` entry resolves to `cloak`. A sandbox can only allow/deny; masking (show structure, hide values) is exclusive to this layer and survives both sandbox tiers.

read.description: Glob -> mask. Pattern matches the resolved file path.

permissionValue.description: allow: proceed; deny: block with policy reason; ask: prompt Yes/No (auto-deny when no UI); cloak: proceed but redact via matching mask (read tool only).

oneOf.description: Glob pattern -> permission. Longest matching pattern wins; ties resolve by insertion order. Patterns use picomatch (dot:true; bash commands also match `/`).

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match sensitive values in the read output.

replace.description: Replacement template (uses native JS replace semantics, e.g. "$1"). When omitted, matches are replaced with asterisks of equal length.
